combat_history.event: India signed a ~US$375M deal to export shore-based BrahMos to the Philippines; deliveries began in 2024.
combat_history.significance: India's first major missile export and a marker of Indo-Pacific arms diplomacy.

combat_history.event: An Indian BrahMos was accidentally fired and landed in Pakistan, causing no casualties.
combat_history.significance: Highlighted the missile's range and the risks of handling supersonic weapons.

modernization.description: Longer-range variants and a lighter next-generation missile for wider platform carriage.
modernization.impact: Broadens reach and the number of launch platforms.

vulnerabilities.description: Large, expensive missile limits magazine depth versus cheaper subsonic weapons.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: BrahMos-NG aims to shrink size and cost.

vulnerabilities.description: Supersonic cruise is detectable before the sea-skimming terminal phase.
vulnerabilities.context: Networked defences may engage if they react fast.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Low terminal altitude and high speed.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Anti-ship and land-attack strikes from land batteries, ships, submarines and Su-30MKI aircraft.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Indian Navy destroyers/frigates, Army coastal regiments, IAF Su-30MKI.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Mature, in service across all three Indian services and exported.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Both are supersonic anti-ship missiles; BrahMos is multi-platform and exported, the YJ-12 is China's air/coastal supersonic ASCM.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: India vs China's supersonic anti-ship missiles.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: BrahMos derives from the Russian Oniks/Yakhont; India added guidance and variants.
Tomahawk is subsonic, longer-ranged and land-attack-focused; BrahMos trades range for supersonic speed.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Speed vs reach in cruise missiles.

doctrine.role: Multi-platform supersonic cruise missile for anti-ship and land-attack strike across all three Indian services.
doctrine.employment: Fire-and-forget Mach-3 attack from land, sea, sub and air; steep-dive and mountain-strike profiles.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Supersonic speed and versatility — one missile family for every domain.
doctrine.threat_context: Anchors India's precision strike in the Indian Ocean and Himalayas; exports project Indian influence into Southeast Asia.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's YJ-12 and the subsonic Tomahawk.
